speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger. To begin my evaluation, how long has this swelling and pain been occurring, and was the onset sudden or gradual?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like a significant trauma mechanism. Did you hear a "pop" or "snap" at the moment of injury, and are you currently able to move your finger or make a fist?

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray right hand (AP, Lateral, Oblique) to rule out fracture or dislocation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand - No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Lag of the Distal Interphalangeal Joint).

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
